dataset_family: UTHealth Houston Neurocognitive Disorders Center Fitbit pilot (Jan 2022-Sep 2023): 12 cases (11 amnestic MCI + 1 early AD) and 8 spouse controls, US
method_family: Consumer wearable passive sensing (Fitbit Charge 4 activity, heart-rate zones, sleep stages); per-participant summary features; SHAP-based fold-wise feature selection; CatBoost (aggregation) / SVM (daily); repeated 5-fold CV and LOOCV
what_it_shows: A consumer Fitbit Charge 4, worn at home for up to a month between two clinic visits, gives AUC 1.0 (repeated 5-fold CV and LOOCV) for clinically diagnosed MCI (n=12, one early AD) vs spouse controls (n=8). This uses the combination of activity, heart rate and main sleep. The purely behavioural channels are lower: activity 0.58 (LOOCV) / 0.76 (5-fold), main sleep 0.77/0.81, activity + main sleep 0.84/0.87. Only AUC is reported in the article body. Accuracy appears only in supplementary tables that are not in the extract.
why: Xu et al. 2024 (JMIR Formative Research 8:e55575). The PDF title, authors and DOI match the block and the map entry. Against Table A1 it matches 'consumer-grade' (Fitbit Charge 4, 'cost-effective, widely available', p.2). It matches 'self-administered' only in the sense of self-worn passive capture: a coordinator set up the device, and staff phoned participants to recharge it (p.3, p.8). It matches 'high standalone discrimination' for a clinically diagnosed target (neurologist diagnosis, MCI due to AD; p.3). It does not show a behavioural instrument. The data are passive activity and sleep, and the best model needs heart rate (physiological). It also does not report accuracy: the ~88-94% band is an accuracy band, while this study prints AUC, and its best result (1.0) sits outside the band. Hence 'partly'. On the narrowed wording, it fits 'low-cost data captured without specialist hardware', 'small internally validated sample', 'no external validation' and 'no head-to-head'. It fits the best-case accuracy strand only partly, for three reasons. (a) The metric is AUC, not accuracy. (b) The perfect separation depends on the physiological heart-rate channel; the behavioural-only combinations give AUC 0.84-0.87 with main sleep, or 0.93-0.97 with naps in only 15 participants. (c) The estimate is optimistic by construction. Features were selected per training fold, then pooled across folds (kept if they appeared in >=2 of 5 folds), and the final models were re-cross-validated on the same 20 participants with those pooled features (p.4). The algorithm and the modality combination were also chosen on the same CV results (p.4-5). Other caveats: n=20. Controls are the cases' spouses, all White, with a significant sex imbalance (P=.03). One case is early AD rather than MCI. The authors themselves list small sample size and possible selection bias (p.8). Independence: a US single-clinic sample (UTHealth Houston; Xu, Kim, Chung, Schulz, Gottlieb). No overlap with I-CONECT or the P-76/P-77 authors, none with P-101, none with the other candidates.

quotes.quote: In this pilot study, fitness trackers were worn by 20 participants: 12 patients with MCI and 8 age-matched controls. We collected physical activity, heart rate, and sleep data from each participant for up to 1 month and further developed a machine learning model to predict MCI status. Results: Our machine learning model was able to perfectly separate between MCI and controls (area under the curve=1.0).
Using cost-effective, widely available fitness trackers (Fitbit Charge 4), we captured sleep, physical activity, and heart rate.

The recruited cohort included 12 cases, including 11 patients with amnestic MCI and 1 diagnosed with early AD. Additionally, 8 age-matched healthy controls were recruited. All the recruited controls were spouses of the recruited MCI
Each participant wore their fitness tracker between 2 consecutive visits to the clinic, returning it during their next visit.

We conducted independent feature selection on each training fold (alpha=0.02) and tested them on their respective testing folds. Finally, we identified features as important if they appeared in at least 2 of the 5 folds.
The final aggregation and daily models were trained using only the features selected in the feature selection stage.

Adding data modalities increases the accuracy of the algorithm, and the combination of physical activity, heart rate, and main sleep achieved perfect separation (AUC=1.0; Table 2; Figure 2; Figure S3 in Multimedia Appendix 1).

The primary limitation of our pilot study is our small sample size and the limited racial diversity in our population.
